records.text: The 工 headword calls the graph pictographic and identifies its referent as a carpenter’s square (曲尺), a tool for drawing right angles or squares. It says the early form’s one-ended box was reduced to a horizontal stroke by late Shang, while earlier Western Zhou bronze forms retained a thick lower stroke that changed through two pictured forms before becoming a thin horizontal. It reports later meanings including artisan, skilled or skillful, engineering, achievement (later written 功), and official or service roles. These are the author’s proposed graphic and semantic account; the graph’s object identification and the proposed sequence are not independently settled by this source.
